sentences.text: This section describes the operational interfaces between the Greenvale Metro Communications-Based Train Control System and station equipment that affects departures, passenger information, and dispatcher awareness.
Platform equipment is treated as part of the movement-authority environment when its state can prevent a train from arriving, dwelling, or departing safely.
Platform Screen Door Controller produces the Platform Door Status Snapshot at each monitored platform face for operational use by the CBTC system.
The door interface reports closed, locked, bypassed, inhibited, and faulted conditions using coded states that are interpreted consistently across the line.
A departure command is not considered available to the Revenue Train Operator until the relevant platform door state is compatible with the requested direction of travel.
North District Zone Controller suppresses platform departure authority when the associated berth reports an unsafe door interface state.
Station status indications presented to local station staff are derived from validated CBTC states rather than from unverified field contacts alone.
These indications distinguish normal service, held train, door interlock fault, radio degraded, emergency stop active, and evacuation support conditions.
The Metro Operations Control System displays station and platform states with the same identifiers used in controller workstations to reduce interpretation errors during incidents.
Passenger Information Gateway receives train prediction data, stopping pattern changes, and platform allocation updates after the CBTC system has reconciled them with the active timetable.
The Passenger Information Gateway shall not publish a revised destination or skip-stop message until the underlying train identity and route have been confirmed by the CBTC system.

When a platform is taken out of service, the passenger information interface marks the affected train movements as unavailable for boarding while retaining their operational tracking in the control center.
Service Timetable Server provides planned service context used to compare predicted arrivals against scheduled platform usage.
Metro Operations Control System coordinates timetable deviation, platform closure, and station crowding information before it is released to passenger-facing systems.
Voice Dispatch Console displays train calling identity, current platform association, and the latest operational hold reason so that spoken instructions match automated indications.
The Line Traffic Controller may apply a station hold through dispatch controls, and the hold is reflected in CBTC departure logic without changing the underlying route locking rules.
Dispatch-related controls use positive confirmation and cancellation states so that a cancelled hold is not confused with a timeout, failed message, or rejected command.
Kestrel shall report train door enable side, berth identity, and departure readiness to support platform interface checks during dwell and dispatch.
Saffron shall maintain message delivery paths for station interface traffic during normal radio coverage transitions and degraded coverage recovery.
Train Radio Modem uses the Encryption Certificate Renewal Pack before accepting renewed secure sessions for passenger-facing and station-interface data paths.
Safety Data Communication Network carries safety-relevant station interface messages separately from nonvital passenger information messages.
Maintenance Diagnostic Server records station interface faults, rejected commands, and inconsistent indications for later investigation by the Signal Maintenance Engineer.
Cyber Security Officer reviews access rights for passenger information and dispatch integration workstations when station-facing interfaces are commissioned or materially changed.
During degraded operation, the CBTC system favours restrictive platform states and requires explicit controller action before restoring automatic departure support at the affected station.
